svg.aria-label: F03 — how the inventory bias scales with aquifer support, and what R-squared says about it
svg.desc: Two stacked panels against aquifer strength, sharing one horizontal axis: terminal water influx as a fraction of the initial hydrocarbon pore volume, from 0 to 0.3303. The upper panel shows the relative error in fitted gas in place rising from about zero at the J equals 0 volumetric control to plus 74 percent at J equals 60, with the remaining-gas error above it at every point, reaching plus 164 percent. The base case, J equals 2, is circled at plus 12.50 percent. The lower panel shows one minus R-squared on a logarithmic scale, rising only from exactly zero at the control, through 1.405e-4 at the base case, to 4.793e-3 at J equals 60 — that is, R-squared falls only from 1.000000 to 0.9952 while the inventory error reaches 74 percent. Each point carries its J value as a direct label. Full values in the table inside this figure and in the data table below it.
